## Rule Cheat Sheet (enforced by the validator)

The following table lists validation rules commonly encountered during extraction. The complete E1‑E15, W1‑W6 definitions are in the [Data Pack Contract](references/data-pack-contract.md).

| Rule | Meaning | Typical triggers |
|---|---|---|
| E1‑E3 | Schema version, meta, and required entity fields (kind, name) | malformed pack, missing `kind` or name-basis |
| E4 | Alias targets must exist in `entities` | crawled name not present in `aliases` → add or map it |
| E5/E7 | References in `relations` or `stages` must resolve to entities (after alias resolution) | **crawled‑name mismatches explode here**; check `aliases` |
| E6/E10 | `relation.type` must be registered in `relationTypes`; attribute labels in `attributeTypes` | undefined relationship enum or attribute label |
| E8 | Stage layout coordinates must be in `[0,1]` | out‑of‑bounds values |
| E11 | Local assets referenced by entities/contents must be registered in `assets` (bare filenames resolved via `meta.assetBase`) | missing asset registration |
| E12 | Multiple edges on the same `(a,b)` pair must be disambiguated by `scope` | two relations between same entities without scope → E12 |
| E13 | Content highlight `ref` must resolve to an entity/alias/annotation key | **wrong entity names in prose are caught** |
| E14/E15 | Both sides of `sameAs` must exist; provenance keys must point at real records | broken equivalence or provenance mismatch |
| W1 | Unreferenced entity (no relations, not in any stage) | intentional singleton or staging missing |
| W2/W4 | Missing asset file or missing hash | integrity concern; only blocks if `--verify-hash` |
| W5 | Below‑threshold confidence (default 0.7) | flags low‑confidence crawled records |
| W6 | Two entities with the same name but no `sameAs` link | possible duplicate → review and add `sameAs` if identical |

**Validation output & strict mode:**
- Without `--strict`: warnings (W*) are recorded but do not cause error exit. The output shows `✔ Validation passed (N warning(s))`. 
- With `--strict`: all warnings become errors, causing exit 1. Use this in CI or final quality gates. 
- When validation fails, the error message includes the rule ID and a short description; consult the contract file for remedies.
